edges.effect_quant: The strongest quantitative studies point in a harmful direction, but the pooled magnitude varies across populations and methods.
edges.population: adults at risk for or living with multiple sclerosis
edges.mechanism: Low vitamin D may weaken immune regulation and tilt toward pro-inflammatory responses relevant to multiple sclerosis susceptibility or activity.
edges.summary: What makes this pair believable is not one flashy paper but the way the literature stacks up: the 2026 Li meta analysis in Front Immunol already points to low vitamin d status tracks with higher risk or worse outcomes, and later studies mostly refine the size of the effect rather than overturning it. In practice this reads more like a real risk signal than a one-off finding.
edges.caveats: Residual confounding and reverse causation remain possible in some observational studies, so the main readout is direction and plausibility rather than one exact risk number.
